The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: 240 {A1} of 240 {A2} shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31 {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-04T02:32:00Z {A4}. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 {A5} days, so the fault is up to that old.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:32:18Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:32:24Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 7 days 18 seconds {alerted_after_the_onset} after the onset.
Broken from 2026-11-04T02:32:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T02:32:54Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 7 days 54 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 35 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:32:54Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - metrics were read, but none from the hour before the onset, so there is no calm level to measure a rise against.
Customer loss: none so far - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:32:18Z {T1.1} Argus: Received SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:32:26Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:32:27Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:32:38Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:32:18 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:32:43Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:32:44Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at Nov 04 02:32 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:32:44Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB, started at Nov 10 14:31:32 {T7.3}, after the onset
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:32:45Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 14 {T8.2} days 8 {T8.3} hours 3 {T8.4} minutes 34 {T8.5} seconds before Nov 11 02:31:34 {T8.6}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:32:46Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:32:47Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:32:47Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 2 {T11.2} candidate causes, best first: C1, C2
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:32:47Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Did not read logs
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:32:48Z {T13.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T13.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T13.3} hour 1 {T13.4} minute before Nov 04 02:33 {T13.5}
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:32:53Z {T14.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:32:53Z {T15.1} Argus: Refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:32:53Z {T16.1} Argus: Left for a person to do - reverting monthly-spend-feature for C1
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:32:54Z {T17.1} Argus: Moved the incident to RECOMMENDED - action recommended
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:35:15Z {T18.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/533

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-04T02:31:32Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - Not read.

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of monthly-spend-feature, each reading it as a different kind of failure - different accounts of what it did, not one cause counted twice - each in its own words:
      C1: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-04T02:31:32Z {C1.1}. From 2026-11-04T02:32:00Z {C1.2} shopper spend totals were written wrong, and all 240 {C1.3} checked totals now disagree with their purchases. The error rate and every latency series stayed at baseline, which is the pattern of silent data corruption. [silent-data-corruption, confidence 0.6 {C1.4}, never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken]
      C2: Switching monthly-spend-feature on at 2026-11-04T02:31:32Z {C1.5} changed how the service computes spend totals, so they no longer reconcile with the purchases behind them. This is the same flag change as the first account, read as a behaviour change rather than as bad values left in the stored totals. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.3 {C1.6}, never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken]

Actions it took:
  - none

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] **The fault.** This is in `src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py`. When `record_a_purchase` is called with `derive_the_month=True`, it sends the write to `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`. That function adds the purchase to the history and moves `total_cents`, but it never writes `total_this_month_cents`. So each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind its purchases. Nothing raises, which matches the flat error rate and latency in the investigation. The investigation ties the corruption to the flag `monthly-spend-feature`. That flag presumably supplies the `derive_the_month` decision, but nothing in this repository maps the flag to that argument, so I could not confirm the link in code.
      
      **The fix.** `record_purchase_deriving_the_month` now writes `total_this_month_cents` as the sum of `price_cents` over the new history's purchases with `in_current_month` true. The account's own stored figure and the account's own purchases therefore agree after every derived write. The flag-off path, `record_purchase`, is unchanged. With the flag on or off, every write leaves `total_this_month_cents` current.
      
      **The test.** I added cases to `tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py`. They record purchases through `record_a_purchase(..., derive_the_month=True)` and assert three things:
      - The stored monthly total includes the new purchase.
      - A purchase from an earlier month leaves the monthly total alone but still moves the lifetime total.
      - After a series of derived writes, `reconcile_monthly_totals` reports no disagreement.
      
      Against the current code the derived path leaves `total_this_month_cents` at its earlier value, so these assertions are written to fail there. Nothing has run them.
      
      **Repair script.** The fix stops new bad writes but does not correct the totals already written wrong. For those I added `scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py`, a one-off script. **It has not been run, and a person has to run it.**
      - It reads account records as JSON lines on stdin and passes them to `reconcile_monthly_totals`.
      - Where the reported gap is positive (the stored total fell behind, the shape this fault produces), it sets `total_this_month_cents` to the sum of that account's current-month purchase prices.
      - Where the gap is negative, it lists the account on stderr and leaves it alone.
      - By default it is a dry run that only reports. Corrected records go to stdout only with `--apply`.
      - Exporting the affected accounts in that shape and loading the output back into the store is left to whoever runs it.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus:
  - [U1] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
  - [U2] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
  - [U3] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
  - [U4] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
  - [U5] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
  - [U6] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
  - Where [F1] says otherwise of these lines, they stand.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
  - AI-2 (mitigate, open): Revert monthly-spend-feature
Rewriting what the incident wrote wrong is left to a person by design: say it in still_at_risk and the action items, never under went_wrong.
PR #533 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1] - suspected, not confirmed.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: When `record_a_purchase` is called with `derive_the_month=True`, it hands the write to `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to the history and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`, and raises nothing. Each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind the purchases that `reconcile_monthly_totals` adds up. The files Code-Fix read do not map the flag monthly-spend-feature to `derive_the_month`, so the record does not show that the flag picks this path. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month, so those totals fell further behind with every purchase.
still_at_risk: Monthly spend totals already stored short stay wrong, and while the flag stays on each new purchase can push another shopper's total further behind, so monthly statements and per-item spend averages read from those totals can show wrong figures.
symptom: Stored shopper monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
causal_chain 1: Stored shopper spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them, falling short. The spend-integrity check found this, not a shopper. That check compares each account's stored monthly total with the sum of its current-month purchases. (cites AL1; U4, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus")
causal_chain 2: The totals fell short because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}, just before the onset at {began}, and from then on purchases were not added to the stored monthly total. The windows read held no other change. The metrics read do not reach back before the onset, so the service was never measured healthy with any earlier change in place. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order"; T13, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 2 ruled_out 2: Any other flag change: the flag provider's history shows no other change by anyone but Argus. (cites T13, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: With the flag on, purchases were likely written through a path that moves the shopper's lifetime total but never the stored monthly total. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: The only check that compares stored spend totals with their purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs once every {A5} days, and no faster signal of this disagreement was seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran far more often would have caught the short totals soon after the flag went on, fewer totals would have been written wrong, and a revert could have been confirmed within the time Argus waits.
contributing_factors 2: No check was seen, before the flag went on, that purchases written through the month-deriving path leave the stored monthly total in line with the purchases.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: A reconciliation run against writes through the new path before the switch would have shown the disagreement, and the flag would not have gone on for live purchases.
contributing_factors 3: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert pages nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person would have been on hand to take up the flag revert that Argus left for a person, and could have stopped new short writes sooner.
action_items 1: Run the spend-integrity reconciliation far more often than every {A5} days, for example continuously or on every write, and alert on the first disagreement.
action_items 2: Before any flag that changes how purchases are written is switched on, run the spend reconciliation against writes through the new path, on staging or a small slice of traffic, and block the switch on any disagreement.
action_items 3: Link the SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person.
action_items 4: Rewrite the monthly totals stored short since the onset, for example by exporting the affected accounts and running the repair script proposed in PR #533, first as a dry run and then with --apply, then load the corrected records back into the store.
action_items 5: Look into by hand any account the repair reports with a negative gap (stored total above its purchases), since the repair script leaves those accounts alone.
went_wrong 1: No on-call person was paged for the alert, even though Argus left the flag revert for a person to do.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
